rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is repentance from unbelief and its noblest form; an unbeliever who dies in unbelief is not accepted in repentance from it.
rows.anchor: لأن إيمان الكافر توبة من كفره ، والإيمان أشرف أنواع التوبة

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the verse literally: death alone prevents an unbeliever from converting; the denied repentance is remorse on Judgment Day, while faith before death is accepted.
rows.anchor: أحدهما الأخذ بظاهره وهو أن لا يحول بين الكافر وبين قبول توبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in the Sahih recounts that the Prophet urged Abu Talib to profess God's oneness at death, but Abu Jahl and Ibn Abi Umayya urged him to remain on Abdul Muttalib's religion; his final words affirmed it.
rows.anchor: فقد ثبت في ( الصحيح ) : أن أبا طالب لما حضرته الوفاة دخل عليه النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between the two clauses distinguishes a person who reaches death from one who actually dies an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ويؤذن به عطف { ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار } بالمغايرة بين قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A living convert's inward faith and spoken profession bring him into the Muslim community, strengthening it and making Islam known among unbelievers.
rows.anchor: الإيمان عمل قلبي ، ونطق لساني ، وقد حصل من الكافر التائب وهو حي

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: A second interpretation equates the unbeliever and sinful believer: neither can repent once death approaches; syntax requires reading 'die' as approach death, like other Qur'anic usage.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما : أن الكافر والعاصي من المؤمنين سواء في عدم قبول التوبة

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Advocates of the second interpretation cite Pharaoh's profession of faith while drowning as an instance of faith not being accepted at that moment.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا بقوله تعالى في حق فرعون { حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's case shows that faith after punishment descends is useless; Jonah's people are the exception, and drowning was punishment for Pharaoh and his army.
rows.anchor: فالغرق عذاب عذب الله به فرعون وجنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command coordinates with the warning in 6:51: the Prophet is to stay with those fearing resurrection despite the arrogance of leading polytheists.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله : { وأنذر به الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed relative description suits the ruling better than a pronoun: those who continually invoke God sincerely deserve the Prophet's company as callers to God.
rows.anchor: فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء داعيا إلى الله فأولى الناس بملازمته

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: In Muslim's report, six companions were with the Prophet when polytheists asked him to expel them; Sa'd names himself, Ibn Mas'ud, a Hudhayli, Bilal, and two unnamed men, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال : كنا مع النبيء ستة نفر

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi identifies the four unnamed companions in Sa'd's account as Suhayb, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt.
rows.anchor: وسمى الواحدي بقية الستة : وهم صهيب ، وعمار بن ياسر

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi's fuller account says Quraysh chiefs proposed removing poor believers while they visited and restoring them afterward; the Prophet refused, then agreed to the arrangement hoping they would believe, and the verse came.
rows.anchor: ما رواه البيهقي أن رؤساء قريش قالوا لرسول الله : لو طردت هؤلاء

rows.speaker: ابن ماجة
rows.claim: A report in Ibn Majah, from Khabbab, names al-Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn as the men who made the expulsion request and cause of revelation.
rows.anchor: ووقع في ( سنن ) ابن ماجة عن خباب أن قائل ذلك للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the Ibn Majah attribution unlikely because this is a Meccan verse and the two men came with the Banu Tamim delegation in Medina.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : هو بعيد لأن الآية مكية . وعيينة والأقرع إنما وفدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men may have made a similar request later, and the Prophet answered it with the verse originally revealed about an analogous proposal.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذلك وقع منهما فأجابهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for whether polytheists believe; their account belongs elsewhere, so he must not deprive believers of their rights to secure others' conversion.
rows.anchor: ما عليك من حساب المشركين على الإيمان بك أو على عدم الإيمان شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive in 'their accounting' can mean either the Prophet's reckoning of them or the polytheists' reckoning of believers' poverty and weakness.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه يجوز كون إضافة { حسابهم } من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted predicate with عَلَى conveys obligation or burden and corrects a possible inclination to yield to Quraysh's chiefs.
rows.anchor: و ( على ) فيه دالة على معنى اللزوم والوجوب لأن الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من is redundant for emphasis, specifying the comprehensive scope of the negation under لا.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من شيء } زائدة لتوكيد النفي للتنصيص على الشمول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the predicates is optional because the following indefinite subjects occur under negation; it may convey emphasis or restriction, and al-Kashshaf favors restriction.
rows.anchor: فلا بد له من غرض . والغرض يحتمل مجرد الاهتمام ويحتمل الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the restrictive reading, only God accounts for the believers; the negated account is confined to the Prophet, as in the restrictive reading of 37:47.
rows.anchor: قصر نفي حسابهم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليفيد أن حسابهم على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic example uses أحرزوا for the polytheists' seizure of the Muslims' collected spoils.
rows.anchor: أي أحرز المشركون ما جمعه المسلمون من الغنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse accumulates five emphases: two uses of من, fronting, restrictive wording, and completion by negating the reciprocal account, to utterly disavow yielding to the request.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمع في هذا الكلام خمسة مؤكدات . وهي ( من ) البيانية ، و ( من ) الزائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address indirectly exposes Quraysh chiefs' claim that poor believers kept them from the Prophet; if sincere, they should attend without judging others, as clarified in 6:55.
rows.anchor: ويفيد هذا الكلام التعريض برؤساء قريش الذين سألوا إبعاد الفقراء عن مجلس الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied affirmative counterpart is that each person is accountable for himself; no believer should lose a right to satisfy the Prophet or someone seeking faith.
rows.anchor: كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning resembles the conditional address in which even the Prophet's work would be void if he associated partners with God.
rows.anchor: فيكون الخطاب على نحو قوله تعالى : { لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك } ( الزمر : 65 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal clause indirectly accuses the polytheists of disguising pride as advice, pretending expulsion would win them over while claiming concern for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء } تعريض بالمشركين بأنهم أظهروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is not that both groups' accounts belong to God: that reading is out of context and makes the second clause redundant, unlike Noah's reported statement.
rows.anchor: ثم بهذا يظهر أن ليس المعنى : بل حسابهم على الله وحسابك على الله ، لأن هذا غير مناسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fronting may simply emphasize that the Prophet bears no obligation, since restriction does not clearly fit the believers who invoke God.
rows.anchor: مجرد الاهتمام بنفي اللزوم والوجوب الذي دل عليه حرف ( على )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal clause is added to complete the rationale; the first clause receives priority because its application to the Prophet and the requesters is the main point.
rows.anchor: وإنما جيء بالجملة الثانية لاستكمال التعليل كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated verb is a subjunctive result of the prohibition; repeating expulsion reinforces the command and reconnects it to the later warning after intervening material.
rows.anchor: لإفادة تأكيد ذلك النهي وليبنى عليه قوله { فتكون من الظالمين } لوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may instead answer the preceding negation: do not expel them merely to satisfy their enemies' wish.
rows.anchor: على أنه يجوز أن يجعل { فتطردهم } منصوبا في جواب النفي من قوله : { ما عليك من حسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among wrongdoers follows from expelling believers to please others; the threat also characterizes the requesters as proud people disposed to injustice.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل طردهم ظلما لأنه لما انتفى تكليفه بأن يحاسبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes 'you would be among wrongdoers' the result of the prohibition, with the repeated expulsion clause serving as a resumptive link after a long interruption.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل قوله : { فتكون من الظالمين } منصوبا في جواب النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb القص means relating or informing, as in the discussion of 6:57.
rows.anchor: والقص : الاخبار ، يقال : قص عليه ، بمعنى أخبره ، وتقدم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God was not absent is a concluding gloss: absence conventionally implies ignorance, so it means God knew every circumstance, like the statement of divine presence.
rows.anchor: والغائب ضد الحاضر ، وهو هنا كناية عن الجاهل ، لأن الغيبة تستلزم الجهالة عرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioning communities here concerns whether messengers conveyed the message, not detailed inquiry into sins; it therefore does not conflict with verses denying such questioning.
rows.anchor: لأن المسؤول عنه هنا هو التبليغ والمنفي في الآيتين الآخريين هو السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing follows the account of people's deeds: it manifests exact reward and punishment without injustice, except where God grants forgiveness or raises a rank.
rows.anchor: فلا جرم أشعرت بأن مظهر ذلك العلم وأثره هو الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin in يومئذ replaces an understood genitive: the day when people and messengers are questioned and their deeds recounted.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في قوله : { يومئذ } عوض عن مضاف إليه دل عليه : { فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here weighing means determining each deed's due reward or punishment precisely; a literal created scale that reveals deeds' measures is also possible.
rows.anchor: فالوزن في هذه الآية يراد به تعيين مقادير ما تستحقه الأعمال من الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figurative measure varies with sincerity: a good deed for God differs from ostentation, as jihad for God's word differs from fighting for booty.
rows.anchor: ككون العمل الصالح لله وكونه رياء ، وككون الجهاد لإعلاء كلمة الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report in the two Sahih collections says an enormous, heavy man will weigh no more than a mosquito's wing with God.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي هريرة ، في ( الصحيحين ) : ( إنه ليؤتى بالعظيم السمين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Ra'i's verse uses weighing as a metaphor for considering and managing a matter.
rows.anchor: ويستعار استعارة تمثيلية للتدبير في أحوال ، كقول الراعي : وزنت أمية أمرها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes two expressions as light on the tongue but heavy in the balance, an example of the noun's figurative use.
rows.anchor: ومثل قول النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم ( كلمتان خفيفتان على اللسان ثقيلتان في الميزان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Language about unseen events can only approximate their realities; verbal nouns without an instrument-taking verb are figurative, while noun forms may be literal or figurative and instrument-taking verbs imply a scale or analogy.
rows.anchor: والعبارات في مثل هذا المقام قاصرة عن وصف الواقعات ، لأنها من خوارق المتعارف

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Reports cited from al-Tirmidhi mention the scale in the hadith of the testimony card and in the Prophet's instruction to Anas to seek him at the scale.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في السنة ذكر الميزان في حديث البطاقة التي فيها كلمة شهادة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No report describing the form of the scale is sound according to the author.
rows.anchor: وقد وردت أخبار في صفة هذا الميزان لم يصح شيء منها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-A'mash deny a created scale and understand the weighing as just judgment; most early authorities affirm the literal scale.
rows.anchor: فاثبت ذلك الجمهور ونفاه جماعة منهم الضحاك ومجاهد والأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among later theologians, most Ash'arites and some Mu'tazilites affirm the scale, while some later Ash'arites and most Mu'tazilites follow the judgment interpretation.
rows.anchor: فذهب جمهور الأشاعرة وبعض المعتزلة إلى تفسير الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author regards the disagreement as minor and the evidence as inconclusive: the intended meaning matters more than the instrument.
rows.anchor: والأمر هين ، والاستدلال ليس ببين والمقصود المعنى وليس المقصود آلته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If weighing is metaphorical, الحق means just; if it depicts a scale, it means even and proportionate to deeds. Calling it by a verbal noun intensifies its reality.
rows.anchor: إن كان الوزن مجازا عن تعيين مقادير الجزاء فالحق بمعنى العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clauses explain the weighing's outcome: success follows heavy measures and loss follows light ones.
rows.anchor: فهو تفصيل للوزن ببيان أثره على قدر الموزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy measures metaphorically mean abundant, dominant good deeds; the weighed object is omitted because people ordinarily weigh prized goods whose exact amount matters.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا مستعار لاعتبار الأعمال الصالحة غالبة ووافرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightness is a matching metaphor for the absence of good deeds, reinforced by the balance imagery and the explanation that they wronged God's signs.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا الخفة الشديدة وهي انعدام الأعمال الصالحة لقوله : { بما كانوا بآياتنا يظلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success means obtaining good and attaining what one seeks.
rows.anchor: والفلاح حصول الخير وإدراك المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite form of المفلحون may be generic or refer back to the established description in 2:5.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { المفلحون } للجنس أو العهد وقد تقدم في قوله تعالى : { وأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although من is singular, it generically denotes everyone meeting the condition, allowing plural demonstrative and pronouns.
rows.anchor: وما صدق ( من ) واحد لقوله : موازينه } ، وإذ قد كان هذا الواحد غير معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative signals that their success results from heavy measures; its distance marks abstract, evaluative distance.
rows.anchor: والاتيان بالإشارة للتنبيه على أنهم إنما حصلوا الفلاح لأجل ثقل موازينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun restricts realized success to this group alone.
rows.anchor: وضمير الفصل لقصد الانحصار أي هم الذين انحصر فيهم تحقق المفلحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss is the opposite of profit; losing themselves means losing their own capacities for benefit, like a merchant who wastes all his capital and is ruined by it.
rows.anchor: فإن كل أحد يرجو من مواهبه ، وهي مجموع نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal باء and مصدرية ما link their loss to persistent wrongdoing against the signs; the imperfect evokes repeated past denial, and ظَلَموا includes denying evidence.
rows.anchor: باء السببية ، وما مصدرية أي بكونهم ظلموا بآياتنا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial is injustice because it suppresses evidence whose truth has been established and refuses to act on it.
rows.anchor: تكذيب ما قامت الأدلة على صدقه فتكذيبه ظلم للأدلة بدحضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting بآياتنا gives the signs emphasis.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور في قوله : { بآياتنا } على عامله ، وهو { يظلمون } ، للاهتمام بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage addresses believers who all did good and polytheists devoid of good; mixed believers are outside its purpose and discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: إذ كان الناس يوم نزول الآية فريقين : فريق المؤمنين ، وهم كلهم عاملون بالصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation's term is its collective lifespan, not each member's individual lifespan; the context and singular الأمة support this, while an individual term would name each person or living being.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد في الآية ، بأجل الأمة ، أجل أفرادها ، وهو مدة حياة كل واحد منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا usually marks future time and condition; the prefixed فاء supplies the consequence linkage, and fronting the time phrase emphasizes the appointed term.
rows.anchor: و { إذا } ظرف زمان للمستقبل في الغالب ، وتتضمن معنى الشرط غالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular أجل has generic force, as its attachment to a plural pronoun indicates.
rows.anchor: وإفراد الأجل في قوله : { إذا جاء أجلهم } مراعى فيه الجنس ، الصادق بالكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating أجل instead of using a pronoun reinforces the ruling and makes the clause stand alone like a proverb.
rows.anchor: وأظهر لفظ أجل في قوله : { إذا جاء أجلهم } ولم يكتف بضميره لزيادة تقرير الحكم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms يستأخرون and يستقدمون mean delay and advance, with the extra letters serving emphasis; people cannot alter God's appointed term.
rows.anchor: و { يستأخرون } : و { يستقدمون } بمعنى : يتأخرون ويتقدمون ، فالسين والتاء فيهما للتأكيد

rows.speaker: أبو الشيص
rows.claim: Abu al-Shis's verse depicts being unable to move later or earlier, illustrating the image of being trapped by an unavoidable decree.
rows.anchor: والمقصود أنهم لا يؤخرون عنه ، فعطف { ولا يستقدمون } لبيان أن ما علمه الله وقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they will then be defeated escalates the warning: after wasted spending and defeat at Badr, it foretells the conquest of Mecca and the end of their power.
rows.anchor: فإنهم بعد أن لم يحصلوا من إنفاقهم على طائل توعدوا بأنهم سيغلبهم المسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive leaves the agent implicit because the context makes Muslims obvious; Meccans fought no one else, and Mecca was neutral territory.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الفعل إلى المجهول لكون فاعل الفعل معلوما بالسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks both actual temporal delay and escalation in rank, as it did in the previous clause.
rows.anchor: و { ثم } للتراخي الحقيقي والرتبي مثل التي قبلها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text renews the explicit label unbelievers rather than using a pronoun to intensify denunciation; the poet's repeated naming of the target illustrates this rhetoric.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن الإضمار هنا إلى الإظهار تخريجا على خلاف مقتضى الظاهر

rows.speaker: عويف القوافي
rows.claim: A verse by Uwayf al-Qawafi repeats the name of the criticized person and blame to heighten denunciation, exemplifying the explicit naming.
rows.anchor: كقول عويف القوافي : اللؤم أكرم من وبر ووالده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause identifies unbelief as the reason for their worldly and afterlife punishment and applies to those who have not abandoned it before events arrive.
rows.anchor: وعرفوا بالموصولية إيماء إلى أن علة استحقاقهم الأمرين في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose phrase attaches to their being gathered: separating wicked people from good people is one of the reasons for gathering unbelievers in Hell.
rows.anchor: و { ليميز } متعلق ب { يحشرون } لبيان أن من حكمة حشرهم إلى جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers vocalize ليميز from māza; Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ya'qub, and Khalaf use the intensive form from mayyaza; attributing the action to God makes the readings equivalent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ليميز } بفتح التحتية الأولى وكسر الميم وسكون التحتية الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sensory filth extends metaphorically to moral vileness; here it describes corrupt souls and deeds, as unbelief distorts belief and action while faith leads oppositely.
rows.anchor: والمراد به هنا خسة النفوس الصادرة عنها مفاسد الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من in the phrase 'the wicked from the good' marks separation, as discussed at 2:220.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من الطيب } للفصل ، وتقدم بيانها عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collecting all wicked people together is another reason for Hell: it separates them publicly from the good, exposes concealed unbelief, humiliates them, and makes them suffer as a heap.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود جمع الخبيث وإن اختلفت أصنافه في مجمع واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukm means piling something above what is beneath it, as in the description of clouds at 24:43.
rows.anchor: والركم : ضم شيء أعلى إلى أسفل منه ، وقد وصف السحاب بقوله : { ثم يجعله ركاما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative says their prior traits make them deserving of the description as losers, since they forfeit both worldly and afterlife benefits.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة ب { أولئك هم الخاسرون } للتنبيه على أن استحقاقهم الخبر الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive pronoun is hyperbolic: their loss is so complete that everyone else's loss counts as none by comparison.
rows.anchor: فصيغة القصر في قوله : { هم الخاسرون } هي للقصر الادعائي ، للمبالغة في اتصافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Prophet means obeying him without opposition; the term is figurative here.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { اتبعوه } أطاعوه ولم يخالفوا عليه ، فالاتباع مجازي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hour is a span of time; al-usra is an intensified verbal noun, and the Hour of Hardship is the mobilization for Tabuk, linked to 9:38.
rows.anchor: وساعة العسرة هي زمن استنفار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الناس إلى غزوة تبوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who accepted the call, prepared, and set out followed the Prophet; the later fighting is jihad rather than the following intended here.
rows.anchor: فالذين انتدبوا وتأهبوا وخرجوا هم الذين اتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The almost-deviation concerns some Emigrants and Helpers who nearly considered staying behind before departure, not people already on campaign; the deviation never occurred.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك لا يتصور وقوعه بعد الخروج ، وهذا الزيغ لم يقع ولكنه قارب الوقوع .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كاد has two-subject syntax like كان; its subject is an implicit pronoun of شأن, dramatizing the seriousness of their near deviation.
rows.anchor: واسمها هنا ضمير شأن مقدر ، وخبرها هو جملة الخبر عن ضمير الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the feminine تزيغ; Hamza, Hafs, and Khalaf read the masculine تزيغ, both valid with a broken plural as subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تزيغ } بالمثناة الفوقية . وقرأه حمزة ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف بالمثناة التحتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ziyagh means turning away from the intended path, as in 3:8.
rows.anchor: والزيغ : الميل عن الطريق المقصود . وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later repentance is temporally subsequent and concerns the near-deviating group, while the initial repentance applies to the others as well.
rows.anchor: أي تاب على غير هذا الفريق مطلقا ، وتاب على هذا الفريق بعد ما كادت قلوبهم تزيغ

rows.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
rows.claim: Many exegetes instead take ثم as sequence in the discourse and the later clause as emphasis, with its pronoun covering all Emigrants and Helpers.
rows.anchor: وجوز كثير من المفسرين أن تكون { ثم } للترتيب في الذكر ، والجملة بعدها توكيدا

none: Verse text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the three coordinates with the Prophet in 9:117, repeating the preposition because of distance; these are a distinct group from other stragglers.
rows.anchor: { وعلى الثلاثة } معطوف { على النبي } ( التوبة : 117 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three are known as Ka'b ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabi, and Hilal ibn Umayya, all Ansar who stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse, admitted guilt, were shunned and separated from their wives, then pardoned after fifty nights.
rows.anchor: وهم : كعب بن مالك من بني سلمة ، ومرارة بن الربيع العمري من بني عمرو

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b's long account of the episode is recorded in both Sahih collections and cited by al-Baghawi.
rows.anchor: وحديث كعب بن مالك في قصته هذه مع الآخرين في ( صحيح البخاري ) و ( صحيح مسلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلفوا is the passive of a normally intransitive verb for remaining behind; it can be construed as their leaving themselves behind or, metaphorically, having their case deferred.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون { خلفوا } بمعنى خلفوا أنفسهم على طريقة التجريد

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b explains that they were not left behind from the expedition; rather, the Prophet deferred their cases unlike those whose excuses he accepted.
rows.anchor: فقال : وليس الذي ذكر الله مما خلفنا عن الغزو وإنما تخليفه إيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not leave themselves behind; someone left them waiting without judgment, with the implied agent being either the Prophet or God.
rows.anchor: ليس المعنى أنهم خلفوا أنفسهم عن الغزو وإنما المعنى خلفهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the ruling to the three as persons means it applies to a relevant state inferred from context, as in the prohibition of carrion at 5:3.
rows.anchor: وتعليق التخليف بضمير { الثلاثة } من باب تعليق الحكم باسم الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth seeming cramped is a metaphor for grief and the Muslims' estrangement from them.
rows.anchor: وضيق الأرض : استعارة ، أي حتى كانت الأرض كالضيقة عليهم

rows.speaker: الطرماح
rows.claim: Al-Tirimmakh's verse depicts the earth filling around someone until it appears narrow in his eyes.
rows.anchor: كما قال الطرماح : ملأت عليه الأرض حتى كأنها من الضيق في عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deferred-case interpretation fits the endpoint of their distress; merely lagging behind on the expedition would have no endpoint.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي فسر كعب به هو المناسب للغاية بقوله : { حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial phrase بما رحبت uses باء for accompaniment and ما as a verbal noun: the earth is wide as commonly known.
rows.anchor: والباء للملابسة ، أي الأرض الملابسة لسعتها المعروفة . و { ما } مصدرية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The constriction of their selves metaphorically expresses grief, as Arabic idiom says the sad person's chest narrows and the happy person's expands.
rows.anchor: وضيق أنفسهم : استعارة للغم والحزن لأن الغم يكون في النفس بمنزلة الضيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ظن means certainty here: they knew only God could grant their pardon, turned to Him alone, and awaited His forgiveness, as in 2:46 and 7:66.
rows.anchor: أي وأيقنوا أن أمر التوبة عليهم موكول إلى الله دون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's later acceptance follows their distress; ثم marks temporal delay, not rank, and the clause supplies the answer to إذا.
rows.anchor: و { ثم } هنا للمهلة والتراخي الزمني وليست للتراخي الرتبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose ليتوبوا means that they would persist in repentance and cease wrongdoing, not that they would sin so as to repent.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد ليذنبوا فيتوبوا ، إذ لا يناسب مقام التنويه بتوبته عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing description of God as the Oft-Returning and Merciful is a concluding expression of favor.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن الله هو التواب الرحيم } تذييل مفيد للامتنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable explains worldly enjoyment in 10:23: it lasts briefly, like crops that flourish and then are harvested; the analogy compares two composite scenes.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تتنزل منزلة البيان لجملة { متاع الحياة الدنيا } ( يونس : 23 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive form stresses how quickly worldly life ends and reverses the audience's assumed belief that its beauty will last.
rows.anchor: وصيغة القصر لتأكيد المقصود من التشبيه وهو سرعة الانقضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole of worldly life is compared to flourishing vegetation in its rapid passing and loss of beauty after its peak.
rows.anchor: شبهت حالة الحياة في سرعة تقضيها وزوال نعيمها بعد البهجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain corresponds to the beginning of life in childhood, when hopes of comfort and freshness first arise.
rows.anchor: شبه به ابتداء أطوار الحياة من وقت الصبا إذ ليس ثمة سوى الأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant mixing with water represents the first flourishing of life; the فاء signals how quickly vegetation and life's growth appear, and mixing means proximity before the water dries.
rows.anchor: ولذلك عطف بفاء التعقيب للإيذان بسرعة ظهور النبات عقب المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human and animal food plants represent pleasures enjoyed by people and animals; lofty ambitions resemble human food, low ambitions cattle fodder, as in 47:12.
rows.anchor: منه أصناف يأكلها الناس من الخضروات والبقول ، وأصناف تأكلها الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop's full ornament and growth represents the peak of worldly benefit, abundance, and absorption in pleasure while people forget its end; compare 10:22.
rows.anchor: وهو غاية شبه بها بلوغ الانتفاع بخيرات الدنيا إلى أقصاه ونضوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's أمر is His decree and creation; its arrival means calamities that rapidly dry and destroy the land, while حتى compresses many stages between life's beginning and end.
rows.anchor: وأمر الله : تقديره وتكوينه . وإتيانه : إصابة تلك الأرض بالجوائح المعجلة لها باليبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night or day leaves every time possible for the sudden end, so no appointed interval gives people security.
rows.anchor: ترديد في الوقت لإثارة التوقع من إمكان زوال نضارة الحياة في جميع الأزمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zukhruf means gold and by extension adornment; the land is personified as a woman taking fine clothes and jewelry, supported by 7:31 and Bashshar's poem.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق أخذ الأرض زخرفها على حصول الزينة فيها استعارة مكنية

rows.speaker: بشار بن برد
rows.claim: Bashshar's poem uses the verb خذي for taking ornate clothes and colors, supporting the image of taking adornment.
rows.anchor: وقال بشار بن برد : وخذي ملابس زينة ومصبغات وهي أفخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ازينت derives from تزينت, with ت changed to ز and assimilated, and a connecting hamza added for pronunciation.
rows.anchor: و { ازينت } أصله تزينت فقلبت التاء زايا ؛ لتدغم في الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden command and harvest signal total destruction and threaten unbelievers; the detail that people think they control the land identifies them as the target, like 6:44.
rows.anchor: إشارة لإرادة الاستئصال فهو ينذر بالتهديد للكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being able to control the land metaphorically means continuing to benefit from it and gather its produce.
rows.anchor: أنهم مستمرون على الانتفاع بها محصلون لثمراتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حصيد means harvested crop; calling the land harvested is a rational metaphor for its plants, while لم تغن means it was not inhabited or cultivated.
rows.anchor: والحصيد : المحصود ، وهو الزرع المقطوع من منابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The باء in بالأمس marks time; أمس means any past period here, as غد and يوم can mean the future and present, illustrated by Zuhayr's verse.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأمس في الآية مطلق الزمن الذي مضى لأن أمس يستعمل بمعنى ما مضى

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse contrasts knowledge of today and yesterday with ignorance of tomorrow, supporting أمس as past time.
rows.anchor: وجمعها قول زهير : وأعلم علم اليوم والأمسس قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement about explaining signs generalizes to proofs of God's knowledge, power, and precision; this parable is one such sign and resembles 6:55.
rows.anchor: مثل هذا التفصيل نفصل أي نبين الدلالات كلها الدالة على عموم العلم والقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The لام in لقوم is purposive; reflection means careful consideration, and the passage hints that those who gain no benefit are not reflective people.
rows.anchor: والتفكر : التأمل والنظر ، وهو تفعل مشتق من الفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to the abode of peace coordinates with 10:24; spelling out God instead of saying 'We call' lets the concluding sentence stand independently.
rows.anchor: فعدل فيها عن الإضمار إلى الإظهار إذ وضع قوله : { والله يدعو } موضع ندعو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of God calls is omitted to include everyone; the call consists of commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { يدعو } لقصد التعميم ، أي يدعو كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode of peace is Paradise, whose name was explained at 6:127.
rows.anchor: ودار السلام : الجنة ، قال تعالى : { لهم دار السلام عند ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the call itself is guidance as direction, يهدي here means creating actual guidance; Ash'arites say God creates each act, while Mu'tazilites say He creates readiness to respond to evidence.
rows.anchor: فتعين أن { يهدي } هنا معناه إيجاد الهداية بمعنى آخر ، وهي حصول الاهتداء بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the road that leads to the destination.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم : الطريق الموصل

none: Verse text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account returns to resurrection after discussing idolatry and the Quran; the judgment day exposes both false gods and deniers of resurrection, completing a ring structure.
rows.anchor: فكان مثل رد العجز على الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم is an adverb attached to خسروا: they lose on the day of resurrection; fronting it emphasizes warning and proof of that day's reality.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { يوم } على الظرفية لفعل { خسر } . والتقدير : وقد خسر الذين كذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them 'those who denied meeting God' instead of using a pronoun identifies denial as the cause of loss and links it to the preceding account of shirk.
rows.anchor: للإيماء إلى أن سبب خسرانهم هو تكذيبهم بلقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use first-person plural نحشرهم; Hafs reads third-person يحشرهم, with the pronoun returning to God's name in 10:44.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { نحشرهم } بنون العظمة ، وقرأه حفص عن عاصم بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short-stay comparison is either parenthetical between gathering and recognition or a circumstantial clause describing those gathered.
rows.anchor: إما معترضة بين جملة : { نحشرهم } وجملة { يتعارفون بينهم } ، وإما حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كأن is the softened form of كأنّ; its usually omitted subject is estimated as هم from the preceding pronouns.
rows.anchor: و { كأن } مخففة ( كأن ) المشددة النون التي هي إحدى أخوات ( إن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image compares people gathered after long periods in graves to themselves if they had stayed only a daytime hour.
rows.anchor: والمعنى تشبيه المحشورين بعد أزمان مضت عليهم في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is partitive but not restrictive: day is the familiar reference for a short time, as in the conventional use of رجال and the hadith about an hour of a day.
rows.anchor: و { من النهار } ( من ) فيه تبعيضية صفة ل { ساعة } وهو وصف غير مراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An hour means a span of time, usually a short one, as in the discussion of 7:34.
rows.anchor: والساعة : المقدار من الزمان ، والأكثر أن تطلق على الزمن القصير إلا بقرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison stresses that elapsed time does not prevent resurrection and that people return with their identities; this displays God's power.
rows.anchor: وهذا اعتبار بعظيم قدرة الله على إرجاعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short stay rebuts the polytheists' claim that long burial and bodily change make resurrection impossible, raised in 79:10–11.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من التشبيه التعريض بإبطال دعوى المشركين إحالتهم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتعارفون بينهم is a circumstantial clause: each recognizes the others whom he knew in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي يعرف كل واحد منهم يومئذ من كان يعرفه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual recognition, like the short-stay comparison, shows that they are gathered with their worldly bodies and faculties, further refuting the claim that death destroys resurrection's possibility.
rows.anchor: لتصوير أنهم حشروا على الحالة التي كانوا عليها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their loss becomes clear because they denied resurrection and failed to prepare by accepting the Messenger's call.
rows.anchor: فظهر خسرانهم يومئذ بأنهم نفوا البعث فلم يستعدوا ليومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows 10:46: whether punishment is hastened or delayed is equal to God because the full punishment is in the afterlife; it then answers their taunting about delay.
rows.anchor: والمناسبة أنه لما بينت الآية السالفة أن تعجيل الوعيد في الدنيا لهم وتأخيره سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect صيغة presents their repeated taunt; الوعد means the promised punishment, and asking when it comes means when it will appear.
rows.anchor: وحكي قولهم بصيغة المضارع لقصد استحضار الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question signals impatience and indifference, then indirectly reveals disbelief: demanding a time means they do not expect the threat to arrive.
rows.anchor: والسؤال مستعمل في الاستبطاء ، وهو كناية عن عدم اكتراثهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened event here is punishment in worldly life.
rows.anchor: والوعد المذكور هنا ما هددوا به من عذاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural challenge addresses the Prophet mockingly, as in 15:6 and 25:7; Abu Bakr al-Aswad's verse likewise mocks the claim of resurrection.
rows.anchor: والخطاب بقولهم : { إن كنتم } للرسول ، فضمير التعظيم للتهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may include the Prophet and believers to sow doubt, but only the Prophet is told to answer because he conveyed the warning and believers follow him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخطاب للنبيء وللمسلمين ، جمعوهم في الخطاب لأن النبي أخبر به
